title: Monte Carlo prediction, control, and importance sampling
brief: Average returns to estimate the random walk's values, learn an epsilon-greedy policy on a small grid, and compare ordinary and weighted importance sampling.
hints: Returns come from one backward loop: running = rewards[t] + gamma * running, then G[t] = running.
For first-visit estimates, make a fresh empty set at the start of each episode and skip a state once it is in the set.
The epsilon-greedy row is np.full(A, epsilon / A) with 1 - epsilon added at the first argmax. The rows must sum to one.
In mc_control, break ties among best actions at random with rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(Q[s] == Q[s].max())). With Q = 0 everywhere, argmax always picks action 0 and walks into the top wall.
rho_{t:T-1} for every t at once is np.cumprod(step[::-1])[::-1], where step = pi[states, actions] / b[states, actions].
OIS divides the sum of rho * G by the number of episodes. WIS divides it by the sum of rho.
